basis: Localized inflammatory pseudotumor of lung; plasma-cell content alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.

Inherited sweat-gland dysfunction with elevated sweat chloride in 7/7; clinically significant electrolyte disturbance with hypernatremic dehydration in 5/7.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the lung.
Ovarian stromal neoplasms arise in reproductive tissue; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ is defining.
Inherited lipidosis; intellectual disability and splenic abnormalities are reported, but their frequency and the nature of splenic injury are unspecified.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by PDE6A variants.
Epilepsy defined by recurrent stimulus-triggered seizures; triggering sensory organs are not themselves damaged.
Streptococcal infection of the pharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; cardiac failure and skeletal myopathy each affect roughly a third or more of reported cases. Respiratory failure alone does not establish lung injury.
Chromosome 3 duplication syndromes commonly cause developmental delay/intellectual disability; unspecified duplicated region prevents reliable additional organ assignment.
Facial muscle hypoplasia defines disease. HPO lists renal defects, cortical atrophy and cleft palate/tooth agenesis at 30-79%; cardiovascular defects are 5-29%.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; abnormal visual accommodation occurs in 30-79%. Ear/facial dysmorphism and slender digits do not establish functional injury.
Fructose metabolism disorder; gastrointestinal symptoms alone do not establish tissue damage. Hepatic failure and renal impairment are annotated at 5-29%.
Defining omphalocele involves congenital abdominal-wall failure with herniated viscera; hand malformations are also defining.
Plasma/B-cell neoplasm involving marrow and spleen; hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in 30-79%. Nephropathy and bone lesions are 5-29%.
Brain hemorrhage 3/5 and intellectual disability 2/4; cataracts 2/4; mitral prolapse 4/9. Hypergalactosemia population frequency is uncertain from one tested patient.
Familial congenital clubfoot; associated lower-limb skeletal abnormalities remain within the same axis.
Congenital finger and toe bone/joint malformations with shortened phalanges and immobile interphalangeal joints.
Localized mast-cell/myeloid neoplasm, predominantly cutaneous; extracutaneous lesions, including pulmonary tumors, are rare.
Defining microphthalmia with cysts and limb malformations; facial clefts alone do not specify oral or airway involvement.
Discoid lupus skin disease 4/4; arthritis 1/3. Oral ulcers have only one assessed case; pulmonary infections and bronchiectasis are secondary diagnoses.
Disorder of the patellofemoral joint causing characteristic pain; cartilage damage is not required.
Congenital bilateral index-finger skeletal duplication.
Reactive cutaneous lymphoid proliferation; supplied ancestry identifies an immune-mediated, IgG4-related disease.
